query: Everything that landed since the v2.3 tag needs looking at — does any of it break the conventions we documented in CONTRIBUTING?
We have a coding standards doc nobody reads. Check the last twenty commits against it and tell me where we've drifted.
Go through this branch and tell me whether it actually does what issue #142 asked for. I think we drifted while building it.
There were a lot of small decisions made along the way on this PR. Does the result still match what the ticket described?
Review everything I've changed since main — I want to know both whether it's up to our standards and whether it matches the PRD.
Before I open the PR, audit the diff since commit abc1234 against both the spec and how we write code in this repo.
I just finished the last implementation slice for this spec. Check the diff against the ticket before I hand it off.
The implementation is done and the tests pass, but I want a second pass over the whole change set against the originating issue.
Diff my branch against the point where I forked it and tell me what a reviewer would object to on style grounds.
Look at my working tree diff and find correctness bugs — anything that'll blow up at runtime.
Check the pending changes on this branch for security vulnerabilities — injection, auth bypass, leaked secrets.
This module has grown messy. Extract the duplicated blocks and rename things without changing behavior.
Sweep the codebase for over-engineering and give me a ranked list of what I can safely delete.
Squash these five commits into one and write me a proper conventional commit message for it.
Write tests for this new pricing function before I touch the implementation.
CI is red and I can't tell which tier these failing tests belong in. Get the suite green locally.
Triage this incoming external PR from a contributor and decide whether it's in scope for the project.
Turn what we discussed into a spec with user stories and put it on the tracker.
Explain how git bisect works and when I'd reach for it.
